_comment: Provenance for the OnlineSim adapter. Every endpoint the adapter calls, and
every provider constant it recognises, is recorded here and checked by
tests/test_onlinesim.py against apps/verification/onlinesim.py.
The point is narrow and important: an invented or mistyped path fails the
suite instead of failing a customer's order in production. If OnlineSim
publishes something new, it gets added here first, from the documentation,
and only then used in code.
Captured 2026-09-27 from the vendor's published API documentation at
https://onlinesim.io/docs/api/en/index, rendered from their OpenAPI
description at https://onlinesim.io/openapi_docs/Onlinesim-API-UN/.

why: The documentation also allows ?apikey= as a query parameter. The adapter
uses the header instead, because query strings are routinely written to
proxy logs, browser history and error trackers, and an API key is a
bearer credential - anyone holding it can spend our balance.

documented_but_unused./api/getfreelist: Free shared numbers. Never resold: they are public, so anyone can read the messages.
documented_but_unused./api/rent/tariffsrent.php: Long-term rental. This platform sells single activations only.

_comment: OnlineSim publishes exactly ONE operation state in its documentation:
TZ_NUM_WAIT, in the getState example. Other states plainly exist upstream,
but guessing their names would be inventing an API.
So the adapter maps the one documented state and treats every other value
as PENDING - never as finished. An unknown state can therefore delay an
order but can never make an unfinished one look delivered, and the expiry
sweep settles it. Whether a code has arrived is decided by the presence of
a message, which is observable, rather than by a state name we assumed.

error_codes._comment: From the documented error schemas (commonErrorResponse, getStateMethodError).

response_conventions.error_flag: response holds one of the documented error codes
response_conventions.getState_shape: a bare JSON array of operation objects, not an object

tariffs_shape.countries: object keyed "_<dialcode>", each {name, original, code, pos, other, new, enable}
tariffs_shape.services: object keyed "_<slug>", each {id, count, price, service, slug}

webhook.direction: OnlineSim POSTs to a URL configured in the account profile
_signature_comment: No signature, HMAC or shared secret is documented for this webhook.
It therefore cannot be trusted as a source of truth: anyone who learns the
URL could post a verification code for any operation id.
The adapter does not treat the callback as authoritative. If it is wired up
at all it may only act as a hint to poll getState sooner - the code we show
a customer is always the one we read back from the authenticated API.

_comment: getNum documents no idempotency key. A request that times out after the
provider has issued a number leaves that number reserved and billed with
no id returned to us.
Our own Order.idempotency_key stops a client retry becoming a second
purchase, so the customer is never double-charged. The residual exposure
is ours, not theirs, and it is bounded by the activation price.
Documented on setOperationOk: with no incoming SMS an operation cannot be
closed until this interval has passed. A cancel attempted sooner is
refused, so 'cancel' is not instant and the UI must not promise that it is.

constraints.close_is_final: After closing, that number cannot be ordered or used again.
constraints.pricing_currency: Profile currency, USD by default; locale_price selects it.
constraints.country_identifier: International dial code (7 = Russia, 373 = Moldova), not ISO 3166.

authorisation_status.operator: ONLINE CONNECTION TECH PTE. LTD. (Singapore, UEN 202604203W)

confirmation.quote: according to the terms of use, the API may be integrated into third-party software products. However, your account will be held responsible for all actions taken by users who purchase numbers.
confirmation.concurrency_quote: There is a standard limit in place, but if you need to increase your account's limit, please contact us in this chat, and we will handle your request on an individual basis.

_comment: This is the permission TextVerified refused, and it is the single fact that
makes this provider usable: integrating the API into a third-party software
product is expressly allowed.
It came from support chat rather than a signed agreement, so keep the
transcript and get it repeated by email before relying on it commercially.
A support agent's word is evidence of intent, not a contract amendment.
The same reply confirms clause 5.1.3 in plain words: our account answers for
everything our customers do with the numbers. That is the whole reason the
AUP gate, the abuse flags and the risk scoring exist, and why they must not
be relaxed.
OUTSTANDING: the concurrency ceiling. Support confirmed a standard limit
exists and can be raised case by case, but did not state the number. Until
it is known, capacity is unplanned - this is exactly the figure that made
TextVerified unusable at 1 rising to 4.
